page.layout: One page of running text, printed page number and running head at the top. No marginal notes in the text block. Two verse lines set apart in italics above the text. The left edge of the scan shows a strip of neighbouring page and faint marks at the top right, which are not printed text.

main_text.l: QUAM multis circumfideantur bonis à Domino in Ecclesiâ
eius, & quantam lætitiam in animis nostris ex eo percipiamus, ha-
ctenus satis, iudicio meo, ex verbis Prophetæ
audiuimus. Nam cùm & priuatis singulorum
membrorum officiis, & communibus Dei in
corpus totum Ecclesiæ summisque beneficiis
intus & foris demonstratis, potentissimè Pro-
pheta sè & Ecclesiam prisca suis temporibus
ad hanc lætitiam excitauerit: nos, qui Deum
esse nouimus constantissimum in promissioni-
bus gratiæ, & salutari beneficentia in Ecclesiam
suam, iisdem argumentis vti necesse est, vt con-
firmemur ipsi, & alios in cognitione ac cōscien-
tia eiusdem boni, quo ad eius per nos fieri poteft,
confirmemus.
Atque hæc quidem Christianæ lætitiæ in no-
bis eiusmodi est, vt omnem metum omnem-
que dolorem eximere ex mentibus nostris &
fugate poffit, si eam animo verè concepimus.
Sed quia illius gratiæ virtutisque diuinæ (quæ
in se est absolutissima perfectissimaque) sensus
est in nobis imperfectissimus: propterea visum

page.notes: Catchword "est" (printed "eft") and signature "L 2" at the foot. The left edge strip and the faint marks at the top right are the neighbouring page or show-through and are not transcribed. The large initial Q of QUAM is a decorated letter, transcribed as the plain letter. The verse lines "6." and "7." are italic scripture quotations, set as paragraphs. The printed long s is rendered as plain s in "suam", "si" and "sensus" per the rules, and the printed "fugate" and "poffit" are kept as seen.
